description: Task-first Agent create-and-launch: one accepted request derives a complete Agent definition from the task and starts the first execution through the canonical launch pipeline, backed by a Project default execution configuration with one precedence rule, a task-first Web composer, and `mo agent start`.

tasks.title: Project default execution configuration and the single precedence rule
tasks.description: Add the Project-scoped default execution configuration (Runtime, Model, optional Variant): a nullable `DefaultExecutionConfigJson` column on `ProjectRow` via EF migration, write/read surfaces on the Project grain and routes, and a scoped DB-backed reader. Implement one `ExecutionConfigResolver` (caller hint → Agent definition → Project default, runtime falling back to `opencode`, explicit malformed values never masked) and apply it at the two existing sites: `AgentReadinessService.StructuralGaps` (default resolves `model-missing`/`variant-without-model`; definition errors unaffected; `MatchesCurrentDefinition` compares the resolved tuple) and the definition-first launch resolution in `AgentLauncher`.
acceptanceCriteria: An EF migration adds nullable `ProjectRow.DefaultExecutionConfigJson` with no rewrite or backfill; a deployment with no default configured shows zero behavior change.

`IProjectGrain.SetDefaultExecutionConfigAsync` validates via `AgentConfigSchema`, replaces any prior default on success, and rejects an invalid default (runtime outside opencode/pi or model without `provider/model`) leaving the previous default untouched.

`PUT/PATCH /api/projects/{projectRef}/default-execution-config` uses a closed field set, and `GET /api/projects/{projectRef}` returns `defaultExecutionConfig` (null when unset) so Web and CLI branch without a second endpoint.

`ExecutionConfigResolver` unit tests cover every precedence combination: hint over definition over default, definition over default, default filling a definition gap, runtime defaulting to `opencode`, and an explicitly malformed value never being masked by a lower-precedence source.
`ProjectDefaultExecutionConfigReader` performs one DB read per request scope (cached), not one read per Agent during list hydration; no Agent-domain grain calls `IProjectGrain` for this.

Readiness spec matrix passes: default resolves `model-missing` and `variant-without-model` to `Ready`/`Unknown`; without a default the gaps remain `Needs setup` with their repair; `runtime-invalid` and `model-reference-malformed` persist regardless of default; a default change does not flip a completed execution's conclusion.
Definition-first launch specs prove an Agent Readiness reports launchable dispatches with the model the default resolved, resolved once at launch.
Spec tests for storage (valid replace, invalid rejected, read surface), resolver unit tests, and readiness/launch specs pass; `npm run test:fast` passes.
`docs/agent-sessions.md` (Configure an Agent) documents the Project default and the readiness behavior change.
tasks.output: EF migration, Project default write/read surfaces, scoped default reader, `ExecutionConfigResolver`, updated `AgentReadinessService` and `AgentLauncher` resolution, with passing server spec/unit tests and updated docs.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies `specs/agent-creation-defaults/spec.md#one-project-default-execution-configuration` and `#readiness-rules-for-default-resolved-and-default-missing-definitions`. Do not auto-fill agent configs at edit time (rejected alternative in design D6). The task-first route (T-002) is the third resolver site and consumes this resolver unchanged.

tasks.title: Task-first create-and-launch route with derived definitions and idempotent replay
tasks.description: Add `POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/agent-tasks` (`Api/AgentTaskRoutes.cs`) as an orchestrator over the unchanged canonical launch: validate the closed field set and hints, derive the definition via a new unit-testable `AgentTaskDefinitionFactory` (conflict-free name with deterministic disambiguation, baseline Instructions and description, materialized execution configuration), pre-mint the Agent id deterministically from the idempotency key with crash-window adoption, then delegate to `IAgentLauncher.LaunchIdempotentAsync` and project the standard `AgentSessionLaunchResponse`. Determinable rejections run before create; replay flows through `ResumeIdempotentAsync` with a caller-visible fingerprint.
acceptanceCriteria: A task alone (non-empty prompt, execution configuration resolvable from hints or the Project default) creates exactly one Agent, AgentJob, AgentSession, SessionInput, and AgentTurn; hints (`name`, `runtime`, `model`, `variant`) override derivation while unspecified parts are still derived.

Rejections before create with the spec's error codes: missing `Idempotency-Key` → `idempotency_key_required`; undeclared top-level field → `unsupported_field` naming it; malformed runtime/model hint → validation error; no usable prompt or attachment → `input_required`; all attachments rejected → `input_unusable` with per-file results and unbind rollback; unknown context reference → same status/code as the definition-first route; conflicting caller `name` → 409 `AGENT_NAME_CONFLICT`; unresolvable execution configuration → `execution_config_unresolvable` naming both repairs.

`AgentTaskDefinitionFactory` is deterministic: name derivation (first sentence, ~60-char cap, Unicode-letter preserving) disambiguates `Base`, `Base 2`, … against active, archived, and reserved built-in names case-insensitively; attachment-only tasks derive `Task {short-token}`; baseline Instructions and description are non-empty and identical for identical requests; the materialized `agentConfig` passes `AgentConfigSchema.Validate`; a `CreateAsync` name race re-disambiguates with bounded retries.

The created Agent's Readiness is `Ready` or `Unknown` — never `Needs setup` from missing defaults — and stores the resolved execution configuration so it is self-describing in lists and immune to later default changes.

Replay returns the original outcome: original identities (including `agentId`/`agentName`) for accepted operations, the recorded rejection for rejected ones; a changed prompt/context/attachments/name/hints under the same key → 409 `launch_idempotency_conflict`; a still-converging plan → 503 `launch_setup_pending` carrying the key; a replay of a crashed attempt adopts the pre-minted Agent instead of creating a second one.

The coordinator fingerprint folds caller-visible inputs only (name hint as `AgentRef`; runtime, model, and variant hints via two append-only nullable request fields; prompt/context/attachments/origin/targetId) so replay reconstructs it before any Agent exists; replay spec tests pin `AgentLaunchCoordinatorCodec.Fingerprint` inputs — an added, changed, or removed model/variant hint under the same key is a 409 conflict, and a request with no model/variant hint hashes identically to the pre-change canonical form so definition-first replays in flight across the deploy converge unchanged.

Coordinator-equivalence specs prove the resulting session metadata, source labels, launch-time definition snapshot, workspace/origin binding, and read surfaces are indistinguishable from a definition-first launch of the created Agent, and a later definition-first launch of that Agent shares the pipeline.

The 201 response reuses `AgentSessionLaunchResponse` verbatim with all identities, workspace, status, attachment results, and the four canonical URLs; `sessionUrl` addresses the created AgentSession page.

Server spec tests mirror the `AgentSessionLaunch*Specs` suites (route shape/validation, orphan-free determinable rejections, replay identity/conflict/pending/rejection/adoption) and factory unit tests cover name derivation, disambiguation, reserved names, attachment-only tasks, and determinism; `npm run test:fast` passes.
`docs/agent-sessions.md` (Launch Entry Points) and `docs/agent-api.md` document the route, its closed field set, and the replay contract.
tasks.output: `Api/AgentTaskRoutes.cs`, `AgentTaskDefinitionFactory`, deterministic Agent identity pre-minting/adoption, validation cascade, and replay wiring over the unchanged launcher, with passing server spec and unit tests plus updated docs.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies `#the-request-surface-is-closed-and-validated-before-creation`, `#definition-creation-composes-the-canonical-launch-path`, `#idempotent-replay-follows-the-launch-convergence-rules`, `#the-response-projects-every-participant-identity`, and the creation-derivation requirements of `specs/agent-creation-defaults/spec.md`. A key reused across both routes must surface as a 409 fingerprint conflict (same key space). Determinable rejection re-evaluation on replay matches the definition-first route's convergence boundary. Terminal-rejection rollback after creation is owned by T-003.

tasks.title: Crash-safe rollback of the created definition on terminal launch rejection
tasks.description: Close the post-creation rejection window: the coordinator plan gains one append-only `DefinitionCreatedByLaunch` flag set by the task-first envelope, and `BeginAbortAfterRejectionAsync`'s abort completion — including the reminder-driven crash-recovery path — archives the created Agent via `IAgentGrain.ArchiveAsync` before recording the rejection. The route's synchronous path maps the same rejection to the response; 503 `launch_setup_pending` never archives.
acceptanceCriteria: A composed launch that converges to a terminal rejection after the definition was created records the rejection under the idempotency key and leaves no active Agent from the request; replaying that key returns the recorded rejection and creates nothing.

The plan flag is append-only with Orleans id discipline; a route-process crash between coordinator abort completion and route observation is repaired by the reminder-driven abort path, which still archives the Agent and completes the plan.

Archival (not deletion) preserves the audit trail and attribution principal; the archived name continues to participate in derived-name disambiguation, and a caller-supplied retry against the archived name gets the actionable 409.
503 `launch_setup_pending` responses never trigger archival — the launch may still complete and the caller retries with the same key to the original outcome.
Definition-first launches are unaffected: plans without the flag never archive their Agent on rejection.

Spec tests cover terminal rejection after creation (archive + recorded rejection), the crash window via injected failure and reminder replay, 503 non-archival, replay of the recorded rejection, and a definition-first rejection regression; `npm run test:fast` passes.
tasks.output: Coordinator plan flag, archive-on-abort completion with crash recovery, route rejection mapping, and passing orphan-window spec tests.
tasks.notes: Implements design D7. The coordinator — not the route — owns the archival so a route crash cannot strand an active Agent. Together with T-002's pre-create validation cascade this completes the orphan-free requirement.

tasks.title: Task-first Web session composer and Agents empty state
tasks.description: Reorient `AgentSessionComposerPage` task-first: prompt, attachments, and context render first; Agent selection becomes optional with neutral state "New Agent for this task". Launching without a selection calls a new `startAgentTask` mutation in `entities/agent` posting to `/agent-tasks` with a caller-generated idempotency key; selecting an Agent keeps the untouched definition-first `useLaunchAgentSession`. Inline execution configuration (Runtime + Model, Variant optional) appears only on the create-new path and only when the Project read reports no `defaultExecutionConfig`; success navigates to the returned `sessionUrl`; the Agents empty state leads with the task composer.
acceptanceCriteria: A task alone launches: with no Agent selected and a resolvable execution configuration, the composer submits the task-first request without requiring an Agent selection and lands the user in the running session identified by the returned Session/Job identities.
Selecting an existing Agent submits the definition-first launch for that Agent through the existing mutation, without overriding its execution definition (regression-covered).

Execution-configuration gating reads `defaultExecutionConfig` from the Project surface: with a default, no execution fields render and no hints are sent; without one, the create-new path requires inline Runtime and Model and submits them as hints — never dead-ending in Agent settings. The inline controls never apply to a selected existing Agent.

Rejection feedback is actionable and state-preserving: the launch-feedback taxonomy gains kinds for `execution_config_unresolvable` (naming both repairs) and pending convergence (retry with the same key) alongside the existing conflict and unavailable-server kinds; the entered prompt, attachments, and context references remain in the composer.

Refinement after launch: the launch result and session view expose a path to the created Agent's detail page where name, description, Instructions, and Skills remain editable through the existing definition editor, affecting only later AgentJobs.
The Agents list empty state's primary action routes to the task-first composer (`agent-sessions/new`) with the definition editor demoted to a secondary action.

Web tests extend the composer suite (task-only launch, inline gating on the default read, failure state preservation, empty-state routing, selected-agent regression) and `packages/web` typecheck and tests pass.
`docs/web-ui.md` documents the task-first composer and empty state.
tasks.output: Reordered composer with optional Agent selection, `startAgentTask` entity client, default-gated inline execution configuration, new launch-feedback kinds, refined empty state, with passing web tests and updated docs.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies the remaining `web-agent-task-composer` requirements: `#inline-execution-configuration-when-no-project-default-exists`, `#launch-feedback-navigates-into-the-running-session`, `#refinement-after-launch`, `#the-agents-empty-state-starts-from-a-task`. Whether the inline model input consumes the #556 preview endpoint or free-form `provider/model` input is deferred to #556's rollout; free-form is acceptable here.

tasks.title: CLI `mo agent start` and the task-first documentation pass
tasks.description: Add the task-first startup subcommand `mo agent start` to the `agent` group in `MohistCliCommands.Agent.cs`: no Agent argument; `--prompt`/`--prompt-file` (mutually exclusive via `BodyInputResolver`), `--attach`, `--name`, `--runtime` (opencode|pi), `--model` (`provider/model`), `--variant`, the same context flags as `mo agent launch`, `--project`, `--idempotency-key`, and standard output selection. It sends `X-Mohist-Launch-Origin: cli`, prints via `TableShape.AgentSessionLaunch` in table mode and the raw server response in JSON mode, and exits 0 only for accepted launches including replay. Complete the change's documentation (`docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`) and own the full repository verification gate.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo agent start --prompt "<task>"` in a Project whose default resolves the execution configuration creates one Agent, launches it in the same step, and prints the resulting identities; execution-hint subsets compose with the Project default under the precedence rule.
Flag validation mirrors `mo agent create`/`mo agent launch`: runtime outside `opencode`/`pi` and `--prompt`/`--prompt-file` conflicts are usage failures before any request.

The idempotency-key contract matches `mo agent launch`: an omitted key is generated and printed before the request in table mode, and a retry with the printed key returns the original Agent, Job, Session, Input, and Turn identities without a second launch (spec-tested).
Table output lists agent id, agent name, job, session, input, turn, workspace, status, and the canonical session/transcript/job/observation URLs; JSON mode prints the raw server response unchanged.

Exit behavior: 0 only for accepted launches including idempotent replay; non-zero for every rejection with actionable errors — `execution_config_unresolvable` naming both repairs (`--runtime`/`--model`/`--variant` or configure the Project default), conflicts identified by cause, pending convergence instructing retry with the same key; no local state requires cleanup.
CLI tests mirror `CliAgentCommandSpecs`: flag matrix, key printing, table/JSON shapes, exit codes, and retry guidance; `npm run test:fast:cli` passes.
`docs/cli-reference.md` and `docs/getting-started.md` present task-first as the default first-run path alongside the unchanged definition-first commands; `npm run docs:check` passes.
The full `npm run verify` gate passes (docs, format, build, all tests) — this final coordinated slice owns it.
tasks.output: `mo agent start` subcommand with launch-contract output and exit behavior, completed user documentation, and a passing full `npm run verify` gate.
tasks.notes: Also satisfies `#the-idempotency-key-contract-matches-mo-agent-launch`, `#output-prints-every-participant-identity`, and `#exit-behavior-is-decisive-and-actionable`. Keep JSON mode raw-server-response-only per the spec (`--output json:field` subsets are explicitly out of scope unless users ask). Depends on the full server surface (T-002/T-003) and the web slice (T-004) because it owns the final repository-wide verify gate.
